subject: Post-demo: performance & SLO checklist / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Carter <john.carter@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Hi John / Ayesha —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the performance/SLO items we discussed:

1) Targets you called out during the call:
   - P95 latency target for text generation: <= 200ms (tail requirement clearly important)
   - Sustained throughput target: 1,000 requests/sec for embeddings + generation mix
   - Concurrency target: ~50 concurrent sessions (each with streaming enabled)
   - Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for progressive UI updates (sub-200ms to first-token ideally)

2) What we need to validate on our side / joint validation plan:
   - Run a 30-minute synthetic workload matching your request mix and payload sizes (we’ll provide the harness)
   - Capture P50/P95/P99 latencies, cold-start behavior, and first-token times for streaming
   - Validate end-to-end throughput with KV cache enabled and disabled (to measure cache hit benefit)

3) Attachments: SLO checklist (attached) and our suggested test payloads.

Next steps / mutual action plan (MAP):
   - Redwood: provision an evaluation sandbox (dedicated capacity) + send test harness by EOD Wed (Sep 8) — Rishi & Vivek
   - FintechCo: share representative request traces and expected payload sizes (Ayesha) by Fri Sep 10
   - Joint run window: target week of Sep 13 for the 30-min run; debrief w/ results the following day

Decision criteria you mentioned: meeting latency & first-token time, predictable cost per 1k requests, and no regression in output quality when using quantized model variants.

If that looks right I’ll schedule the sandbox and lock in the MAP milestones.

Best,
Marissa
Director, GTM — Redwood Inference

Attachments: FintechCo_SLO_checklist.xlsx (Excel), latency-benchmarks-20260907.csv (CSV)

From: John Carter <john.carter@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 18:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 1,000 req/sec number is for peak sustained business hours; average during batch jobs is lower (~200 rps). We need the system to handle both profiles.
- Streaming: our UI needs first-token under 250ms for a good user experience. If first-token is 250-350ms we'd like to understand degradation modes (e.g., cold start, long contexts).
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent *users*, but each user can have up to 6 simultaneous streaming calls in some workflows — so planning for ~300 concurrent model sessions is prudent for safety.

We’ll extract representative traces and payloads — Ayesha will own that. Also please include a short note on the quantized model variants you plan to test (which model family and expected accuracy delta).

Thanks,
John
VP Product — FintechCo

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: John Carter <john.carter@fintechco.com>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Hi John / Ayesha —

Great questions — quick technical clarifications and what we’ll include in the sandbox:

- Throughput profiles: we’ll run two workloads in the sandbox — "peak" (1,000 rps sustained for 30 minutes) and "batch" (200 rps with larger payloads). We’ll produce separate reports for each.
- Concurrency: thanks for calling out the 6x per-user multiplier — we’ll provision the sandbox to emulate ~300 concurrent sessions to stress test connection handling and KV cache pressure.
- Streaming first-token: our baseline with the unquantized model is typically ~120–180ms first-token on A100-equivalent infra for 1K token context; quantized variants can add 30–80ms depending on configuration. We’ll surface first-token and time-to-complete distributions.
- Quantized variants: we plan to test int8 and nf4-style quant (we’ll include model family and commit hashes in the results) and measure quality delta on your eval prompts (we’ll run a small evaluation pass).

Attachments included in the sandbox: streaming_requirements_notes.pdf (notes on client-side framing & connection reuse), a simple perf harness (link), and sample config for KV cache TTLs.

Planned deliverables after the run:
  - Full latency histograms (P50/P95/P99) + first-token distribution
  - Throughput stability chart with error rates
  - Cost estimate (per-1k requests) for the validated config and fallback plan if SLA missed

I’ll send the sandbox details and the harness by EOD today; can we lock the joint run window for Tue Sep 14 16:00–16:45 PT?

Cheers,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance & SLO checklist / next steps

Perfect — thanks everyone. Quick MAP milestone summary (I’ll also add these to the HubSpot deal):
- Sep 8 (done): Redwood to provision sandbox + send harness (Rishi)
- Sep 10: FintechCo to share traces & payloads (Ayesha) — in progress
- Sep 14 16:00 PT: Joint performance run (Rishi & Vivek + FintechCo engs)
- Sep 15: Debrief + decision: redeploy config or iterate on quantization if thresholds missed

Decision criteria recap (for clarity):
- P95 generation latency <= 200ms under peak profile OR clear mitigation plan and acceptable trade-offs
- First-token streaming <= 250ms under normal conditions
- Throughput stability with <1% error rate at target load
- Quality regression <= 5% on your eval prompts when using recommended quantized variant

I’ll update HubSpot and send calendar invites for the run. If we hit the MAP milestones, we’ll prepare a short pricing/commit recommendation for Dedicated capacity to match your cost target.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Marissa
Director, GTM — Redwood Inference
